title: Business Requirements Document — Hospital Patient Portal

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Patient Portal is a digital platform designed to facilitate secure communication, information sharing, and administrative interactions between hospital staff and patients. The strategic rationale for this project is to enhance patient engagement, reduce administrative overhead, and ensure strict compliance with healthcare data privacy standards. Due to the absence of a raw source document excerpt, the specific strategic drivers, target user demographics, and operational goals are currently undefined and require stakeholder input to finalize.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body: While the overarching objective is to provide a secure patient portal, specific business objectives and measurable success metrics (e.g., patient adoption rate, reduction in call center volume, time-to-access for medical records) are not specified in the provided source material. These metrics must be established by the project sponsor and clinical leadership to define the project's success criteria.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body: The operational boundaries of the Hospital Patient Portal are currently undefined. The source material does not specify which modules (e.g., appointment scheduling, billing, medical records viewing, secure messaging) are in scope, nor does it delineate out-of-scope features. This section is an open item requiring explicit stakeholder definition to prevent scope creep and ensure alignment with hospital operational capabilities.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body: The specific stakeholders and governance personas for the Hospital Patient Portal are not identified in the source material. Standard healthcare stakeholders (e.g., Chief Information Officer, Chief Medical Officer, Patient Privacy Officer, IT Security Team) are implied by the domain but must be formally assigned roles and responsibilities by the project governance board.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: The system must provide secure, multi-factor authentication for patient access to the portal.
Users must successfully authenticate using MFA; failed attempts must be logged and trigger security alerts.
All Protected Health Information (PHI) must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
Data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256; data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher.
The system must maintain an immutable audit trail of all user actions involving PHI.
Audit logs must be tamper-proof, time-stamped, and retainable for a minimum of 6 years per HIPAA requirements.
The portal must meet strict Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) standards.
System must recover within 1 hour (RTO < 1h) and data loss must not exceed 5 minutes (RPO < 5min) in the event of a failure.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body: The following assumptions are based on the healthcare domain profile: 1) The system will handle Protected Health Information (PHI) subject to HIPAA and GDPR regulations. 2) The system will integrate with existing hospital infrastructure using HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards. 3) The operational constraint of RTO < 1h and RPO < 5min is a hard requirement for business continuity. Specific operational constraints regarding hardware, network bandwidth, or legacy system integration are not provided in the source material and remain open items.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body: The compliance baseline for the Hospital Patient Portal is strictly governed by HIPAA, GDPR (for EU patients), HL7 FHIR, and DICOM standards. Key compliance risks include unauthorized access to PHI, data breaches, and non-compliance with audit trail immutability requirements. The system must enforce AES-256 encryption for PHI at rest and maintain strict access controls. As no specific risk factors were identified in the audit findings, a comprehensive risk assessment must be conducted by the security team to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities in the portal's architecture and data handling processes.
